diagnosis: The customer upgraded to the Business plan mid-cycle and is questioning why the first invoice is higher than the list price. This matches the standard proration pattern: a credit for the remaining old-plan period plus a charge for the new plan can make the first combined invoice differ from list price. No specialist escalation is required per the policy decision.
reply: Thanks for providing invoice INV-88213. The additional lines are most likely proration from the upgrade: when a plan changes mid billing cycle, the invoice can include a credit for the unused portion of the prior plan and a charge for the new plan for the remainder of the cycle. Because of those lines, the first invoice total may differ from the plan list price; subsequent invoices should reflect the plan price unless billing details change again.
